# The Absolute Is True In So Far Forth

What I, William James,[^1] said just now about the Absolute of transcendental idealism is a case in point.[^2] First, I called it majestic and said it yielded religious comfort to a class of minds, and then I accused it of remoteness and sterility.[^3] But so far as it affords such comfort, it surely is not sterile; it has that amount of value; it performs a concrete function.[^4] As a good pragmatist, I myself ought to call the Absolute true 'in so far forth,' then; and I unhesitatingly now do so.[^5]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means]] "William James"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "What I said just now about the Absolute of transcendental idealism is a case in point."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "First, I called it majestic and said it yielded religious comfort to a class of minds, and then I accused it of remoteness and sterility."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "But so far as it affords such comfort, it surely is not sterile; it has that amount of value; it performs a concrete function."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#Pragmatism as Mediator Between Empiricism and Religion]] "As a good pragmatist, I myself ought to call the Absolute true 'in so far forth,' then; and I unhesitatingly now do so."
